summary: InterMaths is a two-year Erasmus Mundus master's in interdisciplinary mathematics. You start at the University of L'Aquila, spend the second semester at Hamburg University of Technology or TU Wien, and the second year on one of six tracks in Vienna, Hamburg, Barcelona, L'Aquila or Nice. Eighteen scholarships waive all fees and pay €1,400 a month. The scholarship deadline is 17 February 2027 at 13:00 CET.
meta_title: InterMaths 2027: Erasmus Mundus applied mathematics scholarship
meta_description: InterMaths gives 18 scholarships with no fees and €1,400 a month for an applied maths master's in Italy, Germany, Austria, Spain and France. Apply by 17 Feb.
covers: No tuition, registration or other mandatory fees, and full insurance. Self-funded students pay €18,000 for two years.
€1,400 a month. Accommodation, travel and living costs come out of it.
18 Erasmus Mundus scholarships for 2027, at least 3 of them for targeted regions, which include Sub-Saharan Africa (Ghana and Nigeria among them).
eligibility: A bachelor's (180 ECTS or equivalent) in mathematics, applied mathematics, physics, engineering or a similar field with a very strong mathematical background, obtained before 15 August 2027.

English at B2, with a certificate no more than four years old. An official medium-of-instruction certificate is fully accepted if you completed at least one year of secondary or university study in English.
how_to_apply: Fill in the online form, open since 6 November 2026, with a photo, a CV, your passport, your English certificate or medium-of-instruction letter, your transcript, a course description on the programme's template and a one-page letter of intent.
Submit by 13:00 CET on 17 February 2027 to be considered for a scholarship. Your two referees must upload their letters by 3 March 2027.
watch_out: Second-year tracks: computational fluid dynamics (Vienna), imaging (Hamburg), decision making and logistics (Barcelona), healthcare modelling and natural disaster modelling (L'Aquila), and stochastics for neural networks (Nice).
Italian embassies may still ask for a B2 certificate for the visa even if the programme accepts your medium-of-instruction letter.
documents: One-page letter of intent and two reference letters
